I am an old woman of 82 years in Phalombe, and my strength is not what it used to be. My small piece of land, less than a quarter hectare, I plant with beans mixed with maize as my parents taught me. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer from the shop — it is too expensive, and beans do not need it so much anyway. I keep my own seeds from last season, and I put a little manure from the neighbor's goats where I can. My grandchildren help me when they can, because bending down is hard for me now.
